brief: Pictet's weekly kickoff recaps a rotation-driven tape, not a broad selloff. Nvidia CEO Huang's resignation on China spy allegations pushed investors out of AI names into cyclicals and select large-cap tech; the S&P 500 still closed +1.4% (first weekly gain in four) and Nasdaq 100 +2.1%. Europe outperformed on falling crude (back to $90-91 on US-Iran breakthrough hopes), earnings and bank M&A, with the STOXX 600 hitting a new all-time high. A hot CPI print (+0.4% headline, +0.3% core) and hawkish Waller comments (backing a 25bp December hike, floating 50bp, and flagging reversal of last year's three insurance cuts) sent the 10-year above 5% and market pricing to 96% odds of a December hike plus 55bp of cumulative hikes through year-end 2027; Friday's PPI then came in cooler (0.3% vs 0.8% prior, 0.4% expected). Pictet's own exposure model cut global equity exposure to a neutral 43% from 70%, driven by a US downgrade to 40%; Europe held at 73% (from 90%). The post-midterm tech-led drawdown (Nasdaq near -15% from peak) is framed as a leadership reset, not a breakdown or contagion, since EPS revisions stay positive. Q3 earnings remain strong with elevated beat rates. Ahead: Nvidia earnings, Anthropic's IPO, Trump-Xi-Putin talks, FOMC minutes.
